_meta.description: The AIOS WP2 curriculum: sections A–E, their 20 modules (A1–E4) with main and secondary competences, the 36 competences, the five WP3-revised learning journeys (Athena, Apollo, Hephaestus, Prometheus, Themis), and the self-assessment items delivered so far. Built from 'AIOS competence mapping' and 'AIOS WP 2 Plan to populate the SAT' (last edit 28 Sep 2026). Loaded when SEED_DATASET=wp2.
_meta.moodle: Every module and journey names a PLACEHOLDER Moodle course (moodleCourseId); links are built from MOODLE_BASE_URL. Replace with the real ids, or give a full moodleUrl, once the Moodle pages exist.
_meta.levels: Each section's four modules are stored as levels 1-4 (A1 = level 1), as the current adaptive assessment expects. In the curriculum they are parallel topics, not difficulty levels. Open question for the team.
_meta.coverage: Mixed coverage values in the source are stored as their first letter until confirmed with the customer: LJ5 B 'M/S' -> M, LJ5 D 'R/M' -> R, LJ6 A 'M/S' -> M.
_meta.gaps: No items yet for A1 and A4; E3 and E4 have one item each. Items of unsupported types are listed in _pendingItems and not loaded. D3.2 is identical to D1.1 in the source.
_meta.sources: The four partner-institution sources come from the earlier curated course list and link to their own web pages, not Moodle. Which competences they build (primarySourceId / competence_secondary_source) is a PROPOSED mapping from their topics and descriptions. Confirm with the customer.

devAuthoredItems.note: Written by the development team as the first examples of the 'judge an example against criteria' type (criteria_check), not by the content team. Pending the content team's approval.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Accountability
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers responsibility for research decisions, transparent documentation, human oversight and institutional accountability in Open Science and AI-supported workflows.

aios.assessment.competence.name: AI Governance and Regulatory Compliance
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers understanding and application of institutional AI policies, governance responsibilities, regulatory requirements, risk-management processes, accountability mechanisms and appropriate expert escalation.

aios.assessment.competence.name: AI Literacy
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers foundational understanding of AI concepts, models, training and inference, major AI system types, generative AI and LLMs, capabilities and limitations, and informed selection and use of AI tools.

aios.assessment.competence.name: AI Transparency, Disclosure and Traceability
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers transparent disclosure and documentation of AI use, including tools/models used, purposes, relevant prompts or task descriptions, outputs accepted or rejected, human corrections, provenance and traceable decision-making.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Anonymization
aios.assessment.competence.description: Maps to privacy, data protection and safe sharing competences, especially when personal or sensitive data cannot be openly released.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Controlled access
aios.assessment.competence.description: Reflects the principle that access should be as open as possible and as closed as necessary, including mediated, restricted or metadata-only access.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Critical thinking
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers judgement, evidence assessment, evaluation of AI outputs, identification of unsupported claims and reflective decision-making.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Data classification
aios.assessment.competence.description: Aligns with the ability to distinguish public, non-sensitive, personal, sensitive, confidential, proprietary, community-governed and restricted data.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Data governance
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers roles, rights, responsibilities, access rules, stewardship, preservation, reuse and institutional decision-making around research data.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Data stewardship for AI
aios.assessment.competence.description: Links research-data stewardship with AI-specific concerns such as bias, training data, documentation, reproducibility, explainability and human validation.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Develop networks
aios.assessment.competence.description: Relates to collaboration, stakeholder engagement, community building, cross-institutional exchange and professional networking for Open Science adoption.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Ethical reasoning
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers ethical judgement, fairness, harm assessment, responsible openness, community rights, AI bias and the distinction between legality and ethical adequacy.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Evaluate research
aios.assessment.competence.description: Maps to research-quality assessment, evaluation of methods, reproducibility, open outputs, documentation and evidence quality.

aios.assessment.competence.name: FAIR and Reproducible AI
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers application of FAIR and reproducibility principles to AI-supported research, including data, code, workflows, documentation, provenance, versions, model/tool information and the conditions required to reproduce or critically inspect AI-assisted processes.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Human Oversight of AI
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers maintaining meaningful human control over AI-assisted activities, critically verifying outputs, correcting or rejecting AI recommendations, defining decision responsibilities and preserving final human judgement and accountability.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Increase impact of science on policy and society
aios.assessment.competence.description: Connects Open Science with public value, policy relevance, societal engagement, knowledge transfer, sustainability and responsible innovation.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Leverage AI
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers the ability to use AI tools productively for discovery, documentation, data analysis, education and communication while preserving human control.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Licensing and privacy literacy
aios.assessment.competence.description: Combines copyright, open licences, access conditions, privacy protection, data protection and safe reuse of research and educational outputs.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Manage intellectual property rights
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers recognition of rights, open licensing, copyright retention, reuse conditions, third-party material and knowledge-sharing constraints.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Manage projects
aios.assessment.competence.description: Relates to planning objectives, resources, timelines, deliverables, risks, quality and implementation logic for Open Science initiatives.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Manage research
aios.assessment.competence.description: Directly maps to research planning, coordination, execution, documentation, quality control and responsible management of research processes.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Manage research data
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers data management plans, storage, metadata, repositories, FAIR principles, preservation, access decisions and reuse.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Mobilise resources
aios.assessment.competence.description: Aligns with identifying and organising human, financial, technical and institutional resources needed to sustain Open Science activities.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Negotiate
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers agreement-building among stakeholders, balancing openness with legal/ethical constraints, and resolving competing institutional interests.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Open Science literacy
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers foundational knowledge of Open Science values, pillars, open access, open data, open methods, infrastructures and societal engagement.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Operate open-source software
aios.assessment.competence.description: Links digital tool use, open-source environments, code reuse, reproducible workflows and open infrastructures.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Problem solving
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers identifying implementation problems, selecting practical solutions, adapting workflows and resolving technical or organisational barriers.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Promote inclusion and diversity
aios.assessment.competence.description: Maps to equity, accessibility, participation, diversity of knowledge systems, inclusive teaching and reduction of digital or knowledge divides.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Promote open access publications
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers repository deposit, open access publishing, copyright retention, publication strategies, metadata and responsible dissemination.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Research data handling
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers collecting, cleaning, documenting, storing, analysing, sharing and preserving research data according to FAIR and ethical principles.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Research ethics and integrity
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers integrity, transparency, consent, responsible conduct, reproducibility, avoidance of misuse and ethical limits of openness.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Research execution and communication
aios.assessment.competence.description: Connects research implementation with communication of methods, uncertainty, results, documentation and public-facing dissemination.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Responsible AI use
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers safe, ethical and accountable AI use, including bias checks, privacy, explainability, citation transparency, human verification and documentation.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Strategic thinking
aios.assessment.competence.description: Relates to institutional planning, long-term priorities, sustainability, stakeholder alignment and Open Science transformation.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Teach in academic or vocational contexts
aios.assessment.competence.description: Maps to teaching, training, facilitation, open pedagogy, OER use, AI-supported education and professional development in HE/VET settings.

aios.assessment.competence.name: Write research documents
aios.assessment.competence.description: Covers drafting, documenting and communicating research plans, data management plans, reports, metadata records, README files and scholarly outputs.

aios.assessment.question.prompt: What is the main purpose of Open Science?

To replace peer review and established research quality assurance processes with unrestricted public participation

aios.assessment.question.prompt: A researcher plans to share interview data as described below. Which data-protection criteria does the plan meet?

content.exhibit:
Sharing plan
- Names are replaced with codes (P01, P02, …); the code key is stored separately.
- Free-text answers are checked for indirect identifiers before release.
- The consent form covers "use in this study" only.
- The data will be published openly on Zenodo.

options.text: Direct identifiers are pseudonymised
The key that links codes to people is kept apart from the data
The risk of indirect identification is assessed
Participants have consented to the planned sharing
Access is restricted in line with the consent and the data's sensitivity
